mirk.title: Mirk
mirk.tagline: A lead-generating website and content platform for a metal-processing plant.
mirk.summary: A ground-up rebuild of the company website for a metal supplier and processing plant in Akko — department pages, local-SEO service areas, a CMS-driven blog and case studies, and an admin panel that routes every inquiry to sales.
mirk.role: Design, full-stack development, CMS and SEO
mirk.challenge: The previous WordPress site was slow, hard to update and undersold the plant’s capabilities. Sales needed a reliable source of inbound leads, and the office team needed to publish content without calling a developer.
mirk.solution: We rebuilt the site on Next.js with Sanity as the content studio, PostgreSQL (via Prisma and Supabase) for leads, newsletter and analytics, and SendGrid for transactional email. The visual design was developed together with the client — a light, industrial palette — and every page was built RTL-first and keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible.
highlights: Department and product pages for laser and plasma cutting, bending, rolling and iron sales
Service-area landing pages for local search across the Western Galilee, Haifa and the Krayot
Blog and case studies edited in an embedded Sanity Studio, with draft previews
Admin panel for inquiries, newsletter subscribers, service areas and activity logs
WhatsApp, Waze and click-to-call shortcuts, with email alerts to the sales team
Full accessibility statement; Hebrew-first with an English version
mirk.result: A fast, statically rendered site the client’s team updates on its own, with every inquiry landing in one place. In Google search, impressions grew 41% across consecutive 28-day periods and the site reached #1 on Google.

digitengo.title: Digitengo
digitengo.tagline: Lead engineer on a multi-tenant AI platform that runs social-media marketing for small businesses.
digitengo.summary: Digitengo writes, schedules and publishes social posts with AI, reports on paid campaigns across Meta and Google Ads, and captures leads — for small businesses and six white-label partner brands. We’ve led its full-stack development since mid-2025.
digitengo.role: Lead full-stack engineer — architecture, features, infrastructure
digitengo.challenge: A fast-growing product originally built by an outside agency: around seventeen Node.js microservices, a Vue front end and Kubernetes infrastructure, with reliability issues and features that had to ship quickly for paying customers and partners.
digitengo.solution: We took over day-to-day engineering across the whole stack — from the Vue app to the services, queues and AWS infrastructure — shipping new product areas while hardening what was already running in production.
highlights: AI post generation and holiday-aware scheduling with OpenAI and Gemini
Paid-campaigns dashboard combining Meta and Google Ads data with leads and revenue into ROI and ROAS
Publishing to Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, plus Meta lead-form capture
White-label tenants on their own subdomains and a public partner API
Cut the onboarding bundle from 2.27 MB to about 0.55 MB gzipped
Hardened the EKS cluster after a node failure and closed a cross-tenant data leak in scheduled jobs
digitengo.result: A more reliable platform that keeps shipping — over 2,600 commits since July 2025 across the front end, services and infrastructure.

alt.full: Digitengo post feed with scheduled AI-generated posts

my-north-food.title: My North Food
my-north-food.tagline: An online store and operations platform for a Galilee food manufacturer — an AI-built codebase we took over and made production-grade.
my-north-food.summary: A food manufacturer operating since 1979 is moving its ordering, deliveries and back office online: a Hebrew storefront with a product catalog and cart, plus dedicated apps for drivers, production stations and management.
my-north-food.role: Codebase takeover, refactoring and full-stack development
my-north-food.challenge: Orders, delivery routes, kitchen tasks and supplier purchasing were managed by phone and on paper. A first version had already been generated with an AI app builder: it worked in parts, but it was hard to change — React errors, a fragile media flow and manual database changes — and the business still needed one system that customers, drivers, kitchen staff and management could each use from their own device.
my-north-food.solution: We took over the existing React and Express codebase and improved it end to end — frontend, backend and database — while the live system kept running. On that foundation we’re building role-based areas: the public storefront and customer accounts, an admin back office, a driver app, station screens for the kitchen and warehouse, and a management dashboard — all on one shared database.
highlights: Refactored an AI-generated codebase across frontend and backend, without taking the system down
Automated database migrations and seed data; fixed React errors, media uploads and startup scripts
Product catalog, cart and order history, with service requests and inquiries
Back office for products, inventory, weekly menus, kashrut certificates and banners
Driver app with delivery lists and digital signatures on handover
Station screens for daily tasks, goods receipt and purchase orders
Management dashboard for orders and weekly planning
AI chat assistant for customer questions
my-north-food.result: The public site is live on the improved codebase, and the operational modules are rolling out in stages — everything that worked before still works.

galil-dashboard.title: Field Organizing Dashboard
galil-dashboard.tagline: An internal dashboard that replaced a tangle of spreadsheets for a regional volunteer organization.
galil-dashboard.summary: A Hebrew, sign-in-protected dashboard that tracks every community in the region — local coordinators, key figures and a history of field events — with Excel import and export so the team can keep working the way it’s used to.
galil-dashboard.challenge: Volunteers were coordinating dozens of communities across two regional councils and several cities from shared spreadsheets that were hard to search, easy to break and impossible to keep in sync.
galil-dashboard.solution: We built a secure Next.js app on Supabase and Prisma that imports the existing spreadsheets, groups communities by council, and lets organizers search, sort and edit figures inline — then export any filtered view back to Excel.
highlights: Communities grouped by regional council, with search across names, coordinators and phone numbers
Inline editing of key figures, color-coded against regional averages
Per-community coordinator lists and an event history with participants and speakers
One-click Excel export of any filtered view, plus a two-sheet export per community
Supabase Auth with server-side checks on every page and API route
Import scripts that seeded the database from the organization’s existing spreadsheets
galil-dashboard.result: One source of truth for the field team, built in a few days.

tor-group.title: TOR Group
tor-group.tagline: A corporate website for an investment-fundraising firm focused on emerging markets.
tor-group.summary: A responsive, multi-language corporate site for a financial-services firm specializing in investment fundraising and international bond issuance — with a growth-themed design, service and team pages, and built-in accessibility features.
tor-group.challenge: The firm needed a credible, modern presence to present its services, process and partners to international investors — in more than one language.
tor-group.solution: We designed and built a Next.js site with next-intl for localization, Framer Motion for restrained animation and a contact form wired to email, structured around the firm’s approach, timing and process.
highlights: Service, approach, timing and process sections built around the firm’s pitch
Multi-language routing with next-intl
Glass-style hero and a growth-themed visual language
Contact form with email delivery, plus Google Analytics
tor-group.result: A polished first impression for investor conversations, live at thetorgroup.com.

reports-manager.title: Reports Manager
reports-manager.tagline: A Windows desktop app that automates complex Excel reporting for a financial-services firm.
reports-manager.summary: An enterprise reporting tool that ingests large Excel workbooks, validates and reconciles the data, and produces finished reports — replacing hours of manual spreadsheet work. Bilingual Hebrew/English interface.
reports-manager.challenge: Analysts were spending hours each cycle copying, checking and reformatting data across large Excel files, and errors were hard to trace.
reports-manager.solution: We built a WPF application on .NET with EPPlus for Excel processing, JWT-secured access and a guided workflow that flags inconsistencies and helps resolve them before reports are generated.
highlights: Batch processing of large Excel workbooks with EPPlus
Automatic error detection with guided resolution
Hebrew/English interface
Secured access with JWT
reports-manager.result: A repeatable, auditable reporting workflow in place of manual spreadsheet work — one that has saved the client more than $1M.

ecommerce-growth.title: 49% more purchase value on 10% less ad spend
ecommerce-growth.summary: Google Ads and Meta for an Israeli e-commerce brand. In August–October, purchase value attributed to Google Ads rose 49% while ad spend fell 10%, and the Meta video campaign doubled its purchases at a 44% lower cost per purchase.
ecommerce-growth.challenge: The brand sells through its own online store and advertises on both Google and Meta. The goal: more online sales from the same budget or a smaller one.
approach: Measured both periods against a single GA4 purchase action, so the comparison is like for like
Switched the product-sales campaigns to bid for new customers only
Rewrote the brand-search ads and expanded the Performance Max asset groups
Shifted budget toward brand search and Performance Max
Ran video and product sales campaigns on Meta, optimised for purchases
ecommerce-growth.result: Compared with May–July, Google Ads brought 49% more attributed purchase value and 56% more attributed purchases on 10% less ad spend, and return on ad spend rose from 3.2× to 5.3×. On Meta, the video campaign went from 57 to 112 purchases and the product campaign from 41 to 117.
ecommerce-growth.footnote: Sources: Google Ads (one GA4-imported purchase action, 90-day click attribution) and Meta Ads Manager (individual campaigns; 7-day click, 1-day view or engagement), {period} vs. {previous}. These are conversions attributed by each platform, not audited orders, and Google and Meta results are reported separately — never added together.

security-leads.title: 53% lower cost per click, 2.7× the clicks
security-leads.summary: Google Ads for a security-systems installer serving homes and businesses. In October we relaunched the account with separate business and private-customer campaigns: clicks rose from 451 to 1,236, the average cost per click fell 53%, and the website form brought in 12 leads.
security-leads.challenge: The installer needed more enquiries from both homeowners and businesses without paying more per click, and the account's lead tracking had to be rebuilt.
approach: Rebuilt lead tracking around a dedicated website-form conversion
Launched separate campaigns for business and private customers
Added a shared negative-keyword list and excluded irrelevant regions
Refreshed ad assets and focused the account's goals on real enquiries
security-leads.result: October brought 1,236 clicks against 451 in September, at an average cost per click 53% lower, plus 12 leads through the website form.
security-leads.footnote: Source: Google Ads, account totals, {period} vs. {previous}. The website-form conversion was created on 17 September, so September has no complete lead baseline and we don't claim a lead-growth figure.

mirk-seo.title: Local SEO for a metal-processing plant
mirk-seo.summary: SEO for mirk.co.il, the metal-processing website we built, with department and service-area pages structured for local search. Over consecutive 28-day periods, Google impressions rose 41%, the site reached #1 on Google and the Nahariya service-area page climbed from 17.4 to 8.3.
mirk-seo.challenge: A new website for a metal-processing plant in Akko had to show up for the company's name and for the services and towns it covers across the Western Galilee.
approach: Department and service pages for each core service — cutting, bending, rolling and iron sales
Service-area landing pages for the Western Galilee, Haifa and the Krayot
Fast, statically rendered pages, Hebrew-first with an English version
Monitoring in Google Search Console, query by query and page by page
mirk-seo.result: Search impressions grew from 1,150 to 1,623 and the average position improved from 16.9 to 15.5. ‘⁧כיפוף פח אלומיניום⁩’ (aluminium sheet bending) moved from position 20.1 to 11.7.
mirk-seo.footnote: Source: Google Search Console, web search, {period} compared with {previous}. Positions are averages for each period, not live rankings, and Search Console data for the site starts on 29 August 2026.

watch-coating-leads.title: 62% more leads for a specialist service
watch-coating-leads.summary: Meta lead-form campaigns for a luxury-watch coating service. In August–October the campaign collected 377 form leads, up from 233 in May–July.
watch-coating-leads.challenge: A niche, premium service: the campaign has to bring a steady flow of enquiries from a small, specific audience.
approach: Instant lead forms on Facebook and Instagram, so people enquire without leaving the app
A separate WhatsApp campaign alongside the lead-form campaign
Results tracked campaign by campaign in Meta Ads Manager
watch-coating-leads.result: 377 form leads in August–October, 62% more than the 233 in May–July.
watch-coating-leads.footnote: Source: Meta Ads Manager, lead-form campaign, {period} vs. {previous}; 7-day click or 1-day view attribution. Leads are submitted forms, not verified sales.

dance-school-whatsapp.title: 3.4× more WhatsApp conversations
dance-school-whatsapp.summary: A click-to-WhatsApp campaign on Meta for a Jerusalem dance school. Conversations started rose from 140 in May–July to 473 in August–October.
dance-school-whatsapp.challenge: For a local studio, a WhatsApp chat is the shortest path from an ad to a conversation about classes.
approach: Click-to-WhatsApp ads that open a chat straight with the studio
Results measured as conversations started, in Meta Ads Manager
dance-school-whatsapp.result: 473 conversations started in August–October, compared with 140 in May–July.
dance-school-whatsapp.footnote: Source: Meta Ads Manager, WhatsApp campaign, {period} vs. {previous}; 7-day click or 1-day view attribution. Conversations are not confirmed registrations, the cost per conversation rose 30%, and the comparison doesn't control for seasonality.

family-law-traffic.title: 2.5× the clicks on the same budget
family-law-traffic.summary: We took over the Google Ads account of a family-law practice on 1 September. In the first month, clicks rose from 938 to 2,369 and impressions grew 4.2×, on the same budget.
family-law-traffic.challenge: A competitive legal market where every click is expensive: the account had to reach more people for the same money.
approach: Extended reach with Performance Max alongside the search campaigns
Kept total spend flat while bringing the cost per click down
Tracked qualifying phone calls (30 seconds or longer) as their own conversion
family-law-traffic.result: September brought 2,369 clicks against 938 in August, at a 60% lower cost per click, and 4.2× the impressions.
family-law-traffic.footnote: Source: Google Ads, account totals, {period} vs. {previous}; cost per click is account spend divided by clicks. More traffic is not yet more clients: qualifying phone calls from ads were 6 in September against 8 in August.

legal-leads.title: 14% more form leads for a law firm
legal-leads.summary: Meta lead-form campaigns for a law firm serving private clients. The main campaign collected 139 form leads in August–October, up from 122 in May–July.
legal-leads.challenge: Legal help is a high-trust decision: the campaign has to bring steady enquiries from people ready to talk to a lawyer.
approach: Instant lead forms aimed at private clients
Tested campaigns with and without Meta's Advantage+ audience expansion
Leads tracked campaign by campaign in Meta Ads Manager
legal-leads.result: 139 form leads in August–October, 14% more than the 122 in May–July.
legal-leads.footnote: Source: Meta Ads Manager, private-clients lead-form campaign, {period} vs. {previous}; 7-day click or 1-day view attribution. Leads are submitted forms, not signed clients.

children.content: This website is not intended for children under 13 years of age. I do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you become aware that a child has provided me with personal information, please contact me immediately.

international.title: International Data Transfers
international.content: Your information may be transferred to and processed in countries other than your country of residence. These countries may have different data protection laws. I ensure appropriate safeguards are in place to protect your information.

changes.title: Changes to This Privacy Policy
changes.content: I may update this Privacy Policy periodically. I will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page and updating the 'Last updated' date. You are advised to review this Privacy Policy periodically for changes.

contact.title: Contact Me
contact.content: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy or wish to exercise your privacy rights, please contact me at:

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro_paragraph_1: is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. I am continually improving the user experience for everyone and applying the relevant accessibility standards.
accessibility.intro_paragraph_2: This website aims to conform to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards to ensure accessibility for users with disabilities.
accessibility.accessibility_initiative_1: I take accessibility seriously and strive to adhere to the
accessibility.accessibility_initiative_2: Level AA standards. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible to people with disabilities.
accessibility.feature_text_resize: Text size adjustment - increase or decrease text size
accessibility.feature_text_spacing: Text spacing adjustment - increase or decrease spacing between letters
accessibility.feature_line_height: Line height adjustment - increase or decrease line spacing
accessibility.feature_invert_colors: Color inversion - invert website colors for better contrast
accessibility.feature_gray_hues: Grayscale mode - convert colors to grayscale
accessibility.feature_underline_links: Link highlighting - underline all clickable links
accessibility.feature_big_cursor: Large cursor - increase cursor size for better visibility
accessibility.feature_reading_guide: Reading guide - highlight current reading line
accessibility.feature_disable_animations: Animation control - disable website animations and transitions
accessibility.contact_us_paragraph: If you encounter any accessibility barriers while using this website, or if you have suggestions for improvement, please don't hesitate to contact me. I value your feedback and am committed to making this website accessible to everyone.
accessibility.accessibility_commitment: I am committed to maintaining and improving the accessibility of this website. Regular accessibility audits are conducted, and updates are made to ensure ongoing compliance with accessibility standards. Your feedback helps me identify areas for improvement and ensure that all users can access and use this website effectively.
